newsitem.title: THAILAND: China the focus for Hoechst's Asian drive.
newsitem.headline: China the focus for Hoechst's Asian drive.

text.p: Current loss-making investments in China will not prevent German-based conglomerate Hoechst AG from spending 2.5 billion marks in Asia by the turn of the century, a senior company executive said on Thursday.

Board member Hoerst Waesche, who has responsibility for the company's growing presence in Asia, told Reuters in an interview Hoechst would increase its investment profile in China, despite current difficulties there.
He said the company currently has six joint ventures operating in China and a further 12 pending approval -- including one just signed this week.
Waesche forecast a further 12 joint ventures will be signed by the turn of the century. Three of the current operational joint ventures are in Shanghai.
"We have decided China will be our top priority to building our position in Asia," he said.
But he said Hoechst was not yet seeing operating profits from the Chinese operations and declined to speculate when the company could hope to see a return on its investment.
The company has established Hoechst China Investment Holding to handle the new ventures in the country. He said Hoechst has a majority stake in most of the China joint ventures.
Waesche said finding and keeping skilled labour, poor infrastructure and financing for joint venture partners had slowed down project development in China, but the problems were manageable.
Hoechst agro-chemical division AgrEvo has two operational joint ventures in place in China, and is set to be one of the company's core areas since agriculture remains the backbone of China's economy.

Hoechst has stated investment targets by 2000 of one billion marks in China, 800 million in the Indian sub-continent and 700 million in countries belonging to the seven-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).
But Waesche said hitting the investment target in India will be difficult.

"India will be much more difficult. I'm very confident about China and ASEAN. In China we will exceed it. I'm not disappointed by this as long as we reach our overall target for Asia and increase our overall position in Asia."
Currently Hoechst derives only 13 percent of its turnover from Asian markets.
